title: Understanding VPS Salary Bands: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay for a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how VPS salary bands compare to the national minimum wage and award rates. Convert hourly pay to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures using a 38-hour week.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, equating to $1,004.90 per week or $52,254.80 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year). For example, $30 per hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For casual employees, add 25% loading before the calculation.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the national minimum wage and VPS salary bands?
faqs.a: The national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for full-time employees. VPS salary bands are set by the Victorian Government and typically start higher, often above $60,000 per year for entry-level roles. They are not directly comparable to award rates but must meet or exceed the minimum wage.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. For a $59,280 annual salary, super would be $7,113.60 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding VPS Salary Bands and Hourly-to-Annual Conversion

When comparing job offers or planning your finances, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is essential. This is especially relevant for roles covered by **VPS salary bands** (Victorian Public Service classifications), which are structured around annual pay points. However, the same conversion method applies whether you are on a modern award, an enterprise agreement, or a contract.

### The Standard 38-Hour Week

In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. Most full-time roles, including those in the VPS, use this as the base. To convert an hourly rate to annual gross pay:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, if your hourly rate is $35.00:
- Weekly: $35.00 × 38 = $1,330.00
- Fortnightly: $1,330.00 × 2 = $2,660.00
- Annual: $1,330.00 × 52 = $69,160.00

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a baseline estimate.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates vs. VPS Salary Bands

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Ombudsman. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum $33.05 per hour.

Modern awards set higher minimum rates for specific industries and occupations. For example, the Health Services Award and SCHADS Award have recent changes effective from October and December 2026 respectively, as noted in the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database.

**VPS salary bands** are set by the Victorian Government and apply to public service roles. They are generally above award rates and are published as annual salary ranges. For instance, a VPS3 band might start at $76,000 per year. To compare, divide the annual band by 52 and then by 38 to get the equivalent hourly rate. This helps you see how your hourly offer stacks up against VPS classifications.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. Do not add the loading yourself if your rate already includes it. Use the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide for more details.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your gross earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For a $69,160 annual salary, super would be $8,299.20 per year, paid by your employer. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy (2%). The tax-free threshold is $18,200. For a $69,160 salary:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000: 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$69,160: 30% = $7,248
- Total tax: $11,268
- Medicare levy (2% of $69,160): $1,383.20
- Net annual pay: $69,160 – $11,268 – $1,383.20 = $56,508.80
- Fortnightly take-home: approximately $2,173.42

Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures, plus estimated tax and super. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
